name: physical-ai
description: Podman Desktop extension for Physical AI robotics development

physical-ai.general.quayNamespace.description: Default Quay.io namespace for browsing and building images

enumDescriptions: Persistent left sidebar listing every destination, with the active page highlighted
Persistent horizontal tab bar listing every destination, with the active page highlighted
No persistent navigation chrome — the Dashboard grid of cards is the hub (original behavior)
physical-ai.general.navigationLayout.description: Navigation layout for the Physical AI extension shell

physical-ai.general.topicPeekTimeoutSeco.description: Timeout in seconds for Topic Monitor Peek (ros2 topic echo --once). Must be a whole number from 1 to 30.

physical-ai.simulation.distro.description: ROS distro for simulation (humble: TurtleBot3 sim; jazzy: sim + noVNC via jazzy-noble preset)

enumDescriptions: ghcr.io/sloretz multi-arch Humble desktop (recommended on Apple Silicon)
docker.io/library/ros:jazzy-ros-base on Ubuntu Noble (multi-arch Quick Start)
docker.io/ros official Jazzy base (amd64 preset, tag :latest)
physical-ai.simulation.baseImage.description: Base image preset for Image Builder builds

physical-ai.simulation.gpuPassthrough.description: On Apple Silicon (arm64), pass /dev/dri into simulation containers and use virtio-gpu rendering when available. Disable to force software rendering (llvmpipe). Ignored on amd64 (always software GL).

physical-ai.simulation.imageAllowlist.description: ENFORCED — a non-empty value here is required for Simulation launch to succeed, not just a suggestion. Comma-separated image refs or repo patterns (e.g. quay.io/ns/ros2-jazzy-sim:noble or quay.io/ns/ros2-jazzy-sim@sha256:…). Empty = default ros2-*-sim* and ros2-*-turtlebot3. Setting a value REPLACES the defaults entirely — list them too (e.g. myimage-sim*,ros2-*-sim*,ros2-*-turtlebot3) if you still want them to launch. Local image content is still trusted once selected, so this is not cryptographic verification — it exists to stop an accidental/mistyped launch, not a determined user.

enumDescriptions: Show all public repositories in the namespace
Show only repositories matching the curated allowlist

physical-ai.catalog.curatedAllowlist.description: Comma-separated Quay repository name patterns for Curated catalog view. Use * as a wildcard (e.g. ros2-*-base,ros2-*-sim*,ros2-humble-turtlebot3).

enumDescriptions: Single-page pipeline: base image (Step 1) and simulation image (Step 2) shown together
Guided chooser: pick whether to build the base image, the simulation image, or both
Layers — compose an image from base OS + hardened + ROS + simulation layers (experimental)
physical-ai.build.layout.description: Layout for the Image Builder page

physical-ai.build.historyLimit.description: Number of recent image builds to remember (tag, arch, duration, and SBOM if one was generated). SBOM text is fetched on demand when expanded, not kept in memory, so a higher limit mainly costs disk space.

physical-ai.openshift.defaultNamespace.description: Default OpenShift/Kubernetes namespace to use when the current kubeconfig context doesn't specify one (the kubeconfig context's own namespace, when present, always takes priority)

physical-ai.openshift.defaultSoftwareRen.description: Default guaranteed CPU count (requests == limits) for the OpenShift sim container on the software-render path. Seeds the Guaranteed CPUs (sim container) field on the Simulation → OpenShift tab, where it can still be adjusted per deploy (including on the GPU path, which defaults to 7). An N-CPU pod only schedules on a node with ≥ N allocatable CPU.

physical-ai.openshift.deployImageAllowli.description: NOT ENFORCED — UI convenience only. Comma-separated image refs or repo patterns (e.g. ros2-*-sim*, or a full ref) to narrow the OpenShift deploy tab's Image picker dropdown. Empty = suggest every genuinely-amd64 local image, regardless of name. Setting a value narrows the SUGGESTIONS only — the field always still accepts and deploys any free-text value, matched or not.
